name: Columbia
why: Portland outdoor company from 1938 — Omni-Heat, Omni-Tech, the Bugaboo — with 21 full-price stores and 142 outlets; the fishing and hunting lines beside the mountain gear.
origin: Founded in 1938 in Portland, Oregon, USA by Paul Lamfrom (Columbia Hat Company) and later run by Gert and Neal Boyle.

notes.tech: Thread proposed 5 (2026-10-10): Omni-Heat (Reflective, Infinity, Helix); Omni-Tech; OutDry Extreme / ODX; Omni-Shade; Omni-Wick; Omni-Freeze; Omni-Shield; Microtemp XF II insulation — owned: Omni-Heat, Omni-Tech, OutDry, Omni-Shade, Omni-Wick, Omni-Freeze, Omni-Shield, Microtemp, Thermarator, TurboDown (Columbia trademarks); licensed fibre brands named in compositions: Tactel, Lycra; share of range 119/667 men's clothing styles name a Columbia technology in title or composition. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.
notes.craft: Thread proposed 2 (2026-10-10): The founding story is dated and placed (Portland, 1938) and checkable on Columbia's own Our Story page, but no product page names a maker, mill or country, and the corporate impact report describes manufacture by 330 third-party Tier 1 vendors with no owned factory. Its technologies are tech, not craft. Seated as proposed, pending ruling.
